title: Just me yapping about how much I loved Pirates! for 1 minute and 48 s...
transcript: I honestly think one of the biggest snubs at this year's Tony nominations was Pirates The Penzance Musical, which only took home a nomination for Best Revival of a musical, but I think was deserving of a whole lot more. This was one of the most fun and delightful experiences that I've had in a theater all season. Features some really phenomenal performances from David Hyde Pierce, Ramin Karimloo, Nick Barasch, Jinx Monsoon. The entire cast is uniformly excellent and all understand the tone of this piece really well, just to say. They really lean into the absurdity of it, and that is also thanks to Scott Ellis's direction and Warren Carlyle's choreography. They also completely re orchestrated the show from an operatic sound to a jazzy, New Orleans inspired score, and it works surprisingly well. Which is why I was so shocked to see them at not in the best orchestrations category. I also know the lyrics weren't eligible for any Tonys, but I do think one of the highlights of the show is just how witty the lyrics are. Like, not to sound Kermodey, but they truly do not write lyrics like this anymore. And listen, I love contemporary musical theater, but I don't think it's that big a hot take to say that. Modern musical theater tends to favor catchy melodies and big belting, and I think often times the lyrics take a backseat to that. The show feels like the perfect antidote to that. The lyrics are So clever. And I just found myself increasingly delighted at each subsequent rhyme. Listen, is it a perfect show? No. The ending doesn't really work for me. There are times when the plot feels a little stalled. But I was never not entertained. And that is the most important part. And I will also say, I think it's really interesting that I know people who are die hard fans of the original operetta. And they loved this new version. And I also know people who do not like the original operetta, and they loved this version. And that, my friends, is the Mark of a good adaptation.
reasoning: Creator calls it one of the most fun experiences of the season, praises cast, direction, orchestrations, and lyrics, and frames minor flaws as not detracting from entertainment. Clear strong recommendation despite acknowledged imperfections.
